subject: SSO / SCIM cutover and service-account policy coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice.murray@fintechinc.com>; ops@fintechinc.com
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Handoff: SSO/SCIM cutover window + service-account policy

Hi Alice / FinTech ops team,

Thanks again for the productive discovery call. We're ready to start the onboarding handoff and want to align on the access controls cutover so there are no surprises during the migration to SSO + SCIM. Key items we need to lock down before cutover:

- SAML metadata exchange and validation
- SCIM attribute mapping and provisioning scope (users vs groups)
- IP allowlist windows for initial sync and smoke tests
- Service-account creation and naming conventions + minimum privileges
- Org-level policies (password recovery overrides, session length)

Neha from our delivery engineering team will lead the technical checklist — cc'd. Jonas will handle rollback/runbook items and I'm the CS owner coordinating schedule and exec alignment.

Proposed next steps:
1) Share SAML metadata (we can accept either metadata URL or file)
2) FinTech confirms a 2-hour maintenance window for initial SCIM sync (propose Wed 2028-11-08 01:00-03:00 UTC)
3) Provide IP ranges for allowlist and whether you prefer CIDR ranges or single IPs
4) Confirm service-account scope (read-only / full-provision)

I'll attach the redwood-service-accounts-guidelines.pdf and a sample SCIM attribute map for your review.

Thanks — looking forward to locking dates.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood-service-accounts-guidelines.pdf, scim_attr_map_v2.csv

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ops@fintechinc.com
Cc: Alice Murray <alice.murray@fintechinc.com>
Date: 2028-11-02T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: SSO/SCIM cutover window + service-account policy

Marissa — thanks, this looks good. A few clarifications from our side before we commit to the window:

- We can produce SAML metadata file and an endpoint for metadata. Will send by EOD Thursday.
- The proposed SCIM sync window on 2028-11-08 01:00-03:00 UTC is ok for engineering but we need a 24-hour notice in our change management system. Can you confirm by Friday 2028-11-03?
- IP allowlist: we have two egress NAT IPs (35.201.100.23 and 35.201.100.24) and a /28 range for some legacy tooling. We can provide CIDR details in the change ticket.
- Service-account scope: We prefer service accounts with a least-privilege model. For initial provisioning give us one service account with write/provision scope and another with read-only for monitoring.

Also, we have a compliance question: will Redwoods' audit logs show which SCIM actions were performed and by which service account? If so, we need to capture that in the ticket for SOC purposes.

Tom
Senior DevOps Engineer
FinTech Inc.

On Thu, Nov 2, 2028 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote: (see above)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice.murray@fintechinc.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechinc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-03T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: SSO/SCIM cutover window + service-account policy — tech checklist and artifacts

Hi Tom / Alice — thanks for the quick responses. A few technical notes and confirmables from the Redwood delivery side:

1) SAML: we can accept either metadata.xml or a metadata URL. When you send metadata, include your IdP's AssertionConsumerService and NameID formats. We'll validate with our staging tenant and share a report.

2) SCIM: attaching scim_attr_map_v2.csv which is our recommended minimal mapping (email => userName, externalId => id, displayName, entitlements => groups). If you provision groups, indicate whether you want group->team mapping in Redwood or prefer group-membership driven role assignment on your side.

3) Service accounts: per Marissa's attachment, recommended naming convention: fintech-sync-sa-<env> and fintech-monitor-sa-<env>. We'll create IAM credentials and rotate every 90 days by default. By default the provisioner SA needs member:create, member:update, member:delete and group:list; monitor SA needs member:read and audit:read. We can pare down permissions if your security team requires it.

4) IP allowlist and smoke tests: for the initial sync we'd like the allowlist to include the two NAT IPs plus Redwood's staging IPs (listed in the attached doc). For smoke tests we'll do a dry-run provisioning on a set of 10 pilot users before full sync. This is non-destructive by default.

5) Audit logs: yes — all SCIM calls from the service account are logged and surfaced in the org activity feed (timestamp, service-account-id, endpoint, payload summary). We will add the audit export to the change ticket for SOC review.

Next actions for the FinTech team:
- Send SAML metadata file or URL by EOD 2028-11-03
- Create a change ticket referencing CS-4178 with the chosen maintenance window and IP CIDRs
- Confirm whether you want group provisioning enabled on day one or staged later

I'll pilot the staging sync once we have metadata and the service account created.

—
Neha Kapoor
Delivery Engineer, Customer Onboarding | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: scim_attr_map_v2.csv

From: Alice Murray <alice.murray@fintechinc.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ops@fintechinc.com
Cc: tom.ellis@fintechinc.com
Date: 2028-11-03T14:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: SSO/SCIM cutover window + service-account policy — approvals and schedule

Thanks — we've opened change ticket FT-8721 and attached the SAML metadata; Tom just uploaded the CIDR ranges to the change. A few notes from our security/compliance reviewer:

- The proposed two-account approach (provisioner + monitor) is acceptable. We require the monitor SA to be limited to read-only and to have a dedicated key per environment.
- For audit purposes, we need a weekly export of SCIM provisioning activity in CSV to our secure SFTP. Can Redwood deliver a scheduled export or should we pull it via API?
- The requested maintenance window works for us but we'll need a 24-hour rollback plan in the ticket (e.g., immediate SCIM stop + revert group mappings).

We can confirm the window after your 24-hour notice; please mark the change ticket FT-8721 as dependent on Redwood's confirmation and add any runbook links.

—
Alice Murray
Head of Platform Security | FinTech Inc.
alice.murray@fintechinc.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice.murray@fintechinc.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-11-06T16:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: SSO/SCIM cutover window + service-account policy — final confirmation and runbook links

Hi all — quick confirmation from Redwood leadership/delivery side before you raise the final change:

- We'll provide the weekly CSV audit export via a scheduled job that pushes to your secure SFTP (we'll need credentials and path). Alternatively, you can pull via our org-activity API; I'll add the OpenAPI snippet to CS-4178.
- We'll create the two service accounts in your staging instance with the naming conventions Neha listed. Keys will be unique per env and rotated per policy; we'll also add a key-rotation entry to the change ticket.
- Runbook: Jonas has uploaded the cutover and rollback runbook to the shared drive (https://drive.google.com/fintech-onboard-docs) — key steps:
  1) Validate SAML metadata in staging (15m)
  2) Provision service accounts and test key auth (20m)
  3) Dry-run SCIM sync for 10 pilot users (30m)
  4) Full SCIM sync and reconciliation (45m)
  5) Post-cutover smoke tests (30m)

I'll confirm the exact UTC window once we have the change ticket status updated and SFTP details for audit export. Marissa — please confirm you will post a final 24-hour notice in FT-8721 after the SAML artifact is validated.

Thanks everyone — this looks ready pending the items above.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Delivery | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: fintech_saml_metadata.xml (to be uploaded to FT-8721), redwood-service-accounts-guidelines.pdf
